time.desc: The ruling party signed an executive order to impose additional tariffs on imported steel and aluminum products, which will take effect in a short period of time and temporarily exempt some allies.

The ruling party has publicly confirmed that it will grant Law P temporary exemptions to some neighboring countries and allies, and uses permanent exemptions as a bargaining chip in trade agreement negotiations.
The ruling party officially canceled Law P exemptions for many traditional allies, triggering the other party to announce countermeasures and initiate dispute settlement procedures.
The first round of large-scale tariff increases against major trade rivals has officially been implemented, and the other parties have simultaneously implemented reciprocal retaliatory tariffs.
In a media interview Country X, the ruling party made it clear for the first time that it was ready to expand tariff coverage of its major trading rivals to almost all imported goods.
The ruling party launched an emergency agricultural aid package to cushion the impact of tariff conflicts on domestic agricultural groups
The ruling party imposes significant hikes in Law P from specific countries and links them to bilateral diplomatic disputes

The second batch of additional tariffs on major trading rivals officially took effect and triggered reciprocal countermeasures. At the same time, the two sides restarted formal economic and trade negotiations but did not see any substantial breakthrough.
The ruling party announced a new round of additional, wider-covering tariff plans on major trade rivals and threatened to further increase the tariffs.
The phone call between the leaders of the two sides sent a signal of easing and prompted the team to start drafting key points of a potential agreement. Market risk appetite rebounded significantly.
The two countries reached a time-limited trade truce during the multilateral summit, suspending the planned escalation of tax increases and expanding procurement in exchange for a negotiation window.
The ruling party threatened to raise existing tariffs and add a new round of tax increases through social media, impacting the final stage of negotiations that were originally scheduled to proceed.
The ruling party reached an agreement with neighboring countries to withdraw countermeasures with Law P but retained the right to resume taxation when imports rise abnormally.

The ruling party announced a phased increase in tariffs on all imported goods from neighboring countries on the grounds of border management, and simultaneously promoted the legislative approval of new regional trade agreements.
The country's large logistics companies sued the government to stop the implementation of technical ban-type trade restrictions related to major trade rivals.
Officials from neighboring countries warn that negotiations on a regional free trade agreement will be difficult to complete if they are forced to pay Law P tariffs
Trade lobbyists point to the legal structure of regional free trade agreements, which give members mutual exemptions from tariffs, as a major obstacle to applying tariffs to neighboring countries.

Economic advisers who advocate protectionism have become popular candidates to replace senior officials who have resigned from the governing body, and their influence in economic decision-making has increased significantly.

The prime ministers of neighboring countries had a phone call with the leader of the ruling party, refuting the suggestion that their country's steel and aluminum might be transported through the Country X channel, emphasizing that its steel and aluminum are used to manufacture tanks and fighter jets of the ruling party.

Minister-level officials from neighboring countries urgently launched intensive lobbying, contacting more than a dozen senior officials from the ruling party to strive for exemption of Law P for their domestic products.

Leaders of the ruling party issued a statement threatening to impose tariffs on an additional US$100 billion of goods in response to the other party’s announcement of a retaliatory list targeting their country’s agricultural products.

Leaders of the ruling party have publicly downplayed the trade war, saying they will always be friends with Country X leaders and predicting that the two sides will reach an agreement on intellectual property rights and reciprocal tariffs

The ruling party's trade advisers and senior financial officials downplayed trade war concerns on news programs, saying that the tariff threat is just a negotiation tactic and has not yet been implemented.

Regional Organization A The chairman promised to retaliate against the removal of exemptions, calling the move unjustifiable, and would impose taxes on the ruling party's goods and file lawsuits with multilateral trade bodies.

The governments of allied countries are deeply disappointed with the decision to cancel exemptions. Their prime ministers plan to raise the matter in person at multilateral summits. The Minister of International Trade said that the tariffs are obviously absurd and does not rule out counterattacks.
